I built the slice code-first. Nothing was compiled or run.

Proto (additive; CRLF line endings kept): RunLedgerService gets `rpc GetRequestSnapshot`. New messages: GetRequestSnapshotRequest{run_id=1, call_seq=2}, PromptSection{label=1, source=2, digest=3, chars=4, text=5} and GetRequestSnapshotResponse{snapshot_json=1, system_sections=2, tools_json=3, dropped=4, tools_truncated=5, system_truncated=6, call_purpose=7}. Every field has a comment. There is no migration.

session-core run_ledger_grpc.rs:
- `get_request_snapshot` is stricter than plain owner-only. It needs `session:read`. It refuses a ZDR caller with `run_inspection`. A service caller, a system-owned run, any other user and an org admin all get NotFound, because the caller's user_id must equal the run's user_id. A non-persistent run and an expired or missing call also get NotFound.
- D3 is applied server-side in the pure function `prompt_sections`. The stored system blob (system messages joined by "\n\n", per `request_capture::system_text`) is split by the manifest's per-message char counts. A piece keeps its text only if it hashes to its manifest sha256, and only if it is not platform. After the first mismatch, no later section gets text.
- The label table `SECTION_LABELS` includes the round A C6 entries. Any unknown or untagged message is platform.
- New switch `SESSION_CORE_REQUEST_INSPECTOR_READ`, default off, strict parser; UNIMPLEMENTED when off.
- Tests:
  - Unit: `inspector_read_off_is_not_served`, `inspector_sections_hide_platform_text_and_show_memory`, `inspector_label_table_classifies_round_a_sections`, `inspector_sections_show_no_text_after_a_mismatch`.
  - DB (`#[ignore]`): `inspector_hides_platform_text`, `inspector_owner_only`, `inspector_reports_dropped`, `inspector_refuses_zdr_bearer`. They seed through the real S6 writer.

model-gateway http_routes.rs (CRLF kept):
- Route `GET /v1/runs/:run_id/requests/:call_seq`. It is 404 while `MODEL_GATEWAY_REQUEST_INSPECTOR` is off. A ZDR bearer gets 403 `zdr_feature_not_supported`/`run_inspection` before anything reaches session-core. Every session-core NotFound, PermissionDenied or Unimplemented maps to one 404, `run_request_not_found`.
- The handler takes the switch as an argument, so tests never touch env.
- FakeRunLedger now implements the new RPC.
- Tests: `inspector_route_serves_the_owner_the_filtered_call`, `inspector_route_off_is_a_404`, `inspector_refuses_zdr_bearer`.

Verevon gateway (BFF): pass-through route `/api/v1/agents/runs/{run_id}/requests/{call_seq}`.

SPA:
- `getRunRequestSnapshot` in run-console-client. It also drops text for any section whose source is platform or unknown.
- `RequestInspector.tsx` behind `VITE_CHAT_REQUEST_INSPECTOR` (strict, off). It has call prev/next, sections, tools, a message manifest table, "Copy request JSON" and the incomplete-record notice. It is mounted in LedgerInspector when the turn has a run id.
- Action contract `chat.inspect_run_request` (model plane, low risk, read-only, not model-executable). Registry count 259 -> 260.

depth_findings.text: Assumed D3 = (b) (platform sections label + digest + length, org/user/memory text, owner only, server-side filter); PROD + OWN must ratify before SESSION_CORE_REQUEST_INSPECTOR_READ or MODEL_GATEWAY_REQUEST_INSPECTOR is switched on.

Gateway and execution-core system messages carry no `name`, so the snapshot manifest's source_tag is empty and every section is classified platform (no text shown). Org, user and memory text appear only after the prompt builders name their slots with the SECTION_LABELS tags. authored_instructions mixes platform and org text and must be split before any part is tagged org.

Section classification trusts the system message `name` from the snapshot manifest. Before switch-on, verify that no user-controlled input (hoisted pins, imported history, client-sent messages) can produce a system message whose name is a label-table tag, or platform text could be shown as user text.

DoD not run: inspect an S6-captured Do run through :8080 with both inspector switches on. Platform sections must show digest only and memory text must show; a second user, an org admin and a service token must get 404; a ZDR-TEST org bearer must get 403 run_inspection.

None of the new tests were run (code-first order). The Rust unit and DB inspector_ tests, the gateway inspector_ tests, and the vitest suite for RequestInspector.test.tsx and action-registry.test.ts all await the guard.
A ledger tool-call record has no model-call sequence number, so the inspector starts at call 1 and steps prev/next. Linking a record to its snapshot needs call_seq or request_id on the live events.
The tool catalogue (names, descriptions, schemas) is returned unfiltered. D3 covers prompt text only, so whether platform tool descriptions count as a product asset is an open PROD question.
